html:
Do you work in acoustics and care about open science?

Whether you develop research software or use it, the Awesome Acoustic list put together by Valentin Le Bescond is worth a look:

https://github.com/Nitnelav/awesome-acoustic

This open-source collection gathers software resources from across many subfields of acoustics.

In Valentin’s words, its mission is to “help the community discover, share and contribute the best open-source acoustics software and resources.”

The main categories are:

  • General Tools: Acoustic Toolbox (a Python library), MoSQITo, Pyfar, PyTTA, friture and others, for general-purpose acoustic processing and visualization.

  • Signal Processing: PyOctaveBand, Acoular, CleanTiPy and others, for spectral analysis, filtering, acoustic source imaging and more.

  • Room Acoustics: Pyroomacoustics, Virtual Acoustics, edg-acoustics, CHORAS, Diffusion and other tools for sound field modeling and reverberation analysis.

  • Environment: NoiseModelling, NoiseCapture, HRISK, Ono Sensor and Code_Tympan, for noise mapping, data collection and health risk assessment.

  • FEM, Materials, Vibrations: Code_Aster, FEniCS, pyOMA2, OURS and others, for vibration modeling and materials analysis.

  • Soundscape: Soundscapy, scikit‑maad and others, for analyzing ecological sound environments and environmental sound.

  • Bioacoustics: BirdNET, BirdNET‑Pi, PAMGuard, AudioMoth, vak, warbleR, Acoupi and others, for acoustic research on birds and marine mammals, including classification and analysis.

  • Databases: Soundata, xeno‑canto, DCASE, the International Soundscape Database, room‑impulse‑responses, BirdSet and other openly available data resources.

  • Music: librosa, pyAudioAnalysis, madmom, audioFlux and others, for audio feature extraction, analysis and processing.

  • Health: tascar, openMHA, Cape4all and others, focusing on hearing aids and assistive devices, hearing research and acoustic scene rendering.

  • Education: Acoucou, SoftwareProfesionalAcustica and other teaching resources in the form of Jupyter notebooks.

  • AeroAcoustics: AeroAcoustics.jl and others, for aerodynamic noise and model analysis.

About the project

  • The list is maintained by Valentin Le Bescond (who goes by Nitnelav online), an acoustics and vibration engineer and software developer who currently works at Université Gustave Eiffel, a French research university.

  • Awesome-acoustic is one of several open-source projects of his; the others include acoustics tools and models such as NoiseModelling, AcousticToolbox, AcousticNode and Eqasim.

  • The list is fully open source under the CC0‑1.0 license, so anyone is free to use it and contribute to it.

How to use it

  • If you are a researcher or engineer working on acoustics, environmental noise, room acoustics, bioacoustics, soundscape analysis or music signal processing, this list is an excellent place to start.

  • To dig into a particular tool, click its name to go to its GitHub page, where you will find documentation, example code and the latest release.

In short

This site brings together open-source projects in acoustics, spanning signal processing, room acoustics, environmental monitoring, bioacoustics, music analysis, hearing health and other subfields. It is a useful reference for anyone in research, teaching or engineering.
